original.description: Objective:To develop a technology independent soft IP (Intellectual Property) core that complies with the aerospace profile of TSN(Time Sensitive Networking).Description:TSN (Time-Sensitive Networking) and TTE (Time Triggered Ethernet) are the two technologies that allow to deliver determinism and quality of service on top of standard Ethernet networks. Since TTE can be considered  relatively closed technology (i.e. proprietary solution, patents pending on the technology), since a few years TSN is emerging as a potential successor of that technology. TSN is IEEE supported set of standards that implements wide range of quality of services (i.e. reliability, determinism, mixed criticality traffic, redundancy, time synchronization) on top of the standard Ethernet protocols. TSN benefits from Ethernet Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) tools/ecosystem, it is free of patents and is being introduced step-by step in industrial applications (automotive/industrial) and aerospace domain (IEEE P802.1DP - TSN for Aerospace Onboard Ethernet Communications). Although TSN is very successful in the automotive/industrial sector, in space applications TSNis still being considered as low TRL technology. Many current and future Exploration and Space Transportationmissions are considering Ethernet-based networks for the data-handling communication bus. Having thistechnology available for future ESA missions is seen as a key driver for future missions. The aim of this activity Is to develop an IP core that contains the core functionalities of Time-Sensitive Networking needed for space applications. Although the set of TSN standards is very wide, there are several on-going activities aiming attailoring of TSN for space applications. Having an TSN IP tailored to space applications could be considered asa key enabler of this technology in future ESA and national missions.The following technical aspects shall be considered:- Development of End-system IP Core. Switch IP core is out of scope of this activity- One or two Ethernet ports shall be supported.- Host integration: AXI4 lite for registers and IP configuration, and AXI4 stream for packet data- The IP shall support 10/100/1000Mbps speeds. 10Gbps is considered optional.- Compatible and configurable with various PHY interfaces (i.e. MII/GMII/RGMIII).- To be developed as technology independent VHDL.- To be implemented and validated in 2 FPGA/ASIC technologies (preferable NG-Ultra/Ultra300 andMicrochip Polarfire).This activity encompasses the following tasks:- TSN IP core requirements identification and development of the high-level architecture of the TSN soft IP core.- Prototype development and integration into a representative Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) based network platform.- Verification and validation targeting high speed use cases- TSN soft IP core release and related documentation.Deliverables: Prototype, Report, SoftwareApplication/Need Date: Exploration and Space Transportation missions. Mission Classification: alpha, beta,gamma, delta

original.description: Objective:  To demonstrate the efficiency of sustainable and biobased resin to produce recyclable, repairable and reusable composite parts compliant with space requirement by out of autoclave process. Description:  The environmental impact of space activitiesis receiving increasing attention across the European space sector. In line with ESA's Ecodesign Policy, future missions are expected to assess their environmental footprint through Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) methodologies and identify solutions that reduce resource consumption, energy usage, waste generation, and hazardous materials. Composite manufacturing processes have been identifiedas a relevant environmental hotspot, notably during the preparation of the EcoStar IOD mission (ESA PrepE 24-P-M-OPS-12), where out-of-autoclave manufacturing using sustainable feedstocks was highlighted as a promising mitigation pathway. At this stage most of the resins are made using petroleum-based feedstock material and the market is mostly led by non-European large entities. Some of the chemical used to produce most of the resins (i.e Bisphenol A) are subject to increasing regulatory scrutiny and may face future restrictions under the European REACH framework, highlighting the need for sustainable and readily available alternative materials. In this work, sustainable European sourced feed stock material shall be used to produced thermosetting resin to be used in combination with carbon fibres to enable composite part manufacturing by out of autoclave process that will exhibit recyclable, repairable and reusable capabilities. This includes extended pot life resin, 100% biobased resin, REACH compliant resin and vitrimer-based resin. Composites based on carbon fibre will be produced using sustainable resin and tested to reach TRL 4 first at sample level and thenat breadboard level representative of existing mature design for space. The activity will also assess the environmental benefits of the proposed materials and processes through LCA, comparing them against conventional composite manufacturing approaches. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Review of the different out of autoclave processes existing for space applications, - - - - - - Review of the commercially available sustainable resins that could be used for out of autoclave processes, Performing a trade-off taking into account materials/processes compatibility, sustainability aspect of the resin, capability to enable composite recycling, reuse and repairability Select at least 2 different out of autoclave processes for further investigation, Development of test plan at sample level to assess the performance of the chosen material and process, Design, produce and test 2 demonstrators based on relevant composite parts for space applications, Perform simplified LCA and Ecodesign trade off and selection.Deliverables:Breadboard, Report
